items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: The fourth record I can't remember; it was by somebody else, Guy Lombardo or somebody.

ctx.x: ...cooking contest. And I went up there with him. And I had always wanted to see his room anyway. I wanted to see exactly how he hunt his clothes, and whether he threw them in the corner or what the hell he did. So I went up with him. And he had a string, a big long string that went to the light from the bed. He'd pull that, and that would turn the light off. And beside him... He had a deal with the milkman that he'd bring a quart of milk and a half-pint of hundred-proof bourbon, Old Schenley bottle and and (?).…

And he had a vendor, as he called it -- a record player. He called it a vendor. It was a little square thing, you know, like this. And he had a stack of records about, oh, almost twelve inches high. The top record was "'Tis Autumn" by Freddie Montague. The second record was "So Rare" by Jimmy Dorsey. The third record was something by Freddie Snickleprints Prisher. And the fourth record I can't remember; it was by somebody else, Guy Lombardo or somebody. And it just kept on going... There wasn't a Count Basie…
